devices.title: Oracle ZFS Storage ZS3-2
facts: The Oracle ZFS Storage ZS3-2 chassis has the following field-replaceable units (FRUs). FRUs are not customer-serviceable and must be replaced by trained Oracle service technicians. [HTML lines 68-68; FRU service restriction; not permission or recommendation for customer replacement.]

PCIe Risers - There are three risers per system, each attached to the rear of the motherboard. Each riser supports two PCIe cards (which are customer-replaceable units (CRUs)). [HTML lines 72-73; Explicit three risers per system and two CRU PCIe cards per riser; legend labels below are not counts.]

Motherboard - The motherboard includes CPU modules, slots for 16 DIMMs, memory control subsystems, and the service processor (SP) subsystem. The SP subsystem controls the host power and monitors host system events (power and environmental). The SP controller draws power from the host 3.3V standby supply rail, which is available whenever the system is receiving AC input power, even when the system is turned off. [HTML lines 78-85; Motherboard/SP context: 3.3V standby rail whenever AC supplied, even while off; not external input rating.]

Power Distribution Board - The power distribution board distributes main 12V power from the power supplies to the rest of the controller. It is directly connected to the connector break out board and to the motherboard through a bus bar and ribbon cable. It also supports a top cover interlock kill switch. The power supplies connect directly to the power distribution board. [HTML lines 90-96; Main 12V distribution, direct PSU-to-PDB connection and top-cover interlock; not AC input or PSU output rating.]

Storage Drive Backplane - The storage drive backplane includes the connectors for the storage drives, as well as the interconnect for the I/O board, power and locator buttons, and system/component status LEDs. The system has an 8-disk backplane. Each drive has an LED indicator for Power/Activity, Fault, and Locate. [HTML lines 101-107; Explicit eight-disk backplane; component LEDs remain source-local.]

Oracle ZFS Storage ZS3-2 CPU and Memory - The Oracle ZFS Storage ZS3-2 controller motherboard has 16 slots in two groups that hold industry-standard DDR3 low voltage (LV) DIMMS. [HTML lines 198-199; Sixteen DDR3 LV DIMM slots in two groups; no installed capacity inference.]
Note: All sockets must be occupied by identical DDR3 DIMMs. [HTML lines 201-205; All sockets must be occupied by identical DDR3 DIMMs; retain alongside the literal component table.]

Oracle ZFS Storage ZS3-2 Storage, Power, and Fan Components - The Oracle ZFS Storage ZS3-2 controller's internal storage, power, and cooling components are described in the following figure and legend. A component identified as a field-replaceable unit (FRU) must be replaced by trained Oracle service technicians. [HTML lines 348-349; Storage/power/cooling figure legend only; FRU service restriction explicit.]

Oracle ZFS Storage ZS3-2 Internal Cables - The Oracle ZFS Storage ZS3-2 controller contains the following field-replaceable unit (FRU) internal cables. FRUs are not customer-serviceable, and must be replaced by trained Oracle service technicians. [HTML lines 437-438; Internal cables are FRUs and not customer-serviceable; no individual cable part numbers printed.]

devices.title: Oracle ZFS Storage ZS3-4
facts: Oracle ZFS Storage ZS3-4 Internal Boards - The Oracle ZFS Storage ZS3-4 controller chassis contains the following field-replaceable units (FRUs). FRUs are not customer-serviceable, and should only be replaced by trained Oracle service technicians. [HTML lines 154-155; Internal board FRUs not customer-serviceable; service-platform name is not merged with registry ZS3-4.]

Motherboard - The motherboard includes CPU modules, slots for eight DIMM risers, memory control subsystems, and the service processor (SP) subsystem. The SP subsystem controls the host power and monitors host system events (power and environmental). The SP controller draws power from the host's 3.3V standby supply rail, which is available whenever the system is receiving AC input power, even when the system is turned off. [HTML lines 159-166; Eight DIMM-riser slots and SP 3.3V standby rail; not external input rating.]

Power Distribution Board - The power distribution board distributes main 12V power from the power supplies to the rest of the system. It is directly connected to the Vertical PDB card, and to the motherboard through a bus bar and ribbon cable. It also supports a top cover interlock ("kill") switch. In the controller, the power supplies connect to the power supply backplane which connects to the power distribution board. [HTML lines 171-178; Main 12V distribution, Vertical PDB interconnect, bus bar/ribbon and top-cover interlock; PSUs connect via PSU backplane (unlike ZS3-2 text).]

Vertical PDB Card - The vertical power distribution board, or Paddle Card serves as the interconnect between the power distribution board and the fan power boards, hard drive backplane, and I/O board. [HTML lines 183-188; Source-local vertical PDB/Paddle Card description; not a new standalone part identity.]

Power Supply Backplane Card - This board connects the power distribution board to power supplies 0 and 1. [HTML lines 193-196; Power supplies 0 and 1 are explicit labels, not a wattage/redundancy specification.]

Fan Power Boards - The two fan power boards are FRUs and carry power to the controller fan modules. In addition, they contain fan module status LEDs and transfer I2C data for the fan modules. [HTML lines 201-205; Explicit two fan power boards, FRU service scope, module LEDs/I2C; no fan-module count inferred.]

Drive Backplane - The six-drive backplane includes the connectors for the drives, as well as the interconnect for the I/O board, Power and Locator buttons, and system/component status LEDs. Each drive has an LED indicator for Power/Activity, Fault, and Locate. [HTML lines 210-215; Explicit six-drive backplane; not installed drive count.]

Oracle ZFS Storage ZS3-4 System Drives - The Oracle ZFS Storage ZS3-4 controller has two system boot drives in slots 0 and 1, configured as a mirrored pair. Read-optimized cache devices can be installed in controller slots 2 through 5, or installed in Oracle Storage Drive Enclosure DE2-24 disk shelf slots. [HTML lines 219-220; Two mirrored boot drives in slots 0/1; read-cache choices remain conditional and constrained by following note.]

Note: Read cache devices must be installed in either the controller or an Oracle Storage Drive Enclosure DE2-24 disk shelf. Read cache devices cannot be installed in both controller and disk shelf slots at the same time. For software requirements and slot configuration rules, see Disk Shelf Configurations. [HTML lines 221-223; Read cache must be in either controller or DE2-24 shelf, never both simultaneously; linked software/slot rules not collected.]

Oracle ZFS Storage ZS3-4 4x4 SAS-2 HBA - The 4x4 SAS-2 HBA, installed in the Oracle ZFS Storage ZS3-4 controller, provides connectivity to external Oracle Storage Drive Enclosure DE2 and Sun Disk Shelves. The HBA logical ports are numbered 3-0, top to bottom: [HTML lines 252-253; Source-local 4x4 SAS-2 HBA connectivity and logical port numbering 3-0; not a new HBA part code.]

Oracle ZFS Storage ZS3-4 CPU and Memory - The Oracle ZFS Storage ZS3-4 controller supports 16GB DDR3 DIMMs installed on all eight risers, accommodating 1TB of memory. [HTML lines 257-258; Source statement supports 16GB DDR3 on all eight risers, accommodating 1TB; no unit configuration claim.]

Refer to the service label on the cover for DIMM placement information. On every memory riser, slots D0, D2, D4, and D6 must be populated; optionally, slots D1, D3, D5, and D7 may be populated as a group on all installed memory risers. All DIMMs in the system must be identical. [HTML lines 260-266; D0/D2/D4/D6 required on every riser; optional D1/D3/D5/D7 as a group on all installed risers; identical DIMMs.]
The following LEDs are lit when a fan module fault is detected: [HTML lines 273-273; Fan-fault introduction; the following three LED blocks belong to this condition.]
Front and rear Service Action Required LEDs [HTML lines 277-277; Fan-fault indication: front and rear Service Action Required LEDs.]
Fan Module Service Action Required (TOP) LED on the front of the controller [HTML lines 282-283; Fan-fault indication: front Fan Module Service Action Required TOP LED.]
Fan Fault LED on or adjacent to the faulty fan module [HTML lines 288-288; Fan-fault indication: Fan Fault LED on or adjacent to faulty module.]

The system Overtemp LED might light if a fan fault causes an increase in system operating temperature. [HTML lines 292-293; Overtemp LED might light if fan fault raises system operating temperature; conditional, not guaranteed.]
